Studies by online video editing platform Kapwing have revealed that almost 60% of TikTok videos are AI slop, while the same is true of 21% of YouTube ones …

TNW reports that the study analyzed more than 10,000 TikTok videos.

The exact percentage was 59%, while an earlier study found that the same was true of 21% of YouTube videos.

This latest study revealed that the problem is even worse when it comes to videos aimed at kids.

The overall percentage of AI-generated content is likely to be even higher, given that the company only identified what it described as “clearly AI-generated scripts and voiceovers.”

The good news is that you can train both platforms to show less of it, as the AI slop levels were at their highest for a new user with no watch history. But those are still pretty terrifying stats, and the problem is only going to get worse.

The site’s Ana Maria Constantin notes that video platforms reward quantity over quality, incentivizing people to upload AI-created content.
